properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, extending Alex's system-of-systems note.

HIS WORDS: *"the graph is the systems engineering 'object' and can have all vertical tiers. However, when a user requests, give me the 'top level management' view, the agent should be able to get the info from the graph and render the user the requested 'view'. I don't know all the DoDAF and UAF views, but there is probably something for 'management' or 'vision'."*

⚠️ **CORRECTED TWICE WITHIN THE HOUR. BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE ON HIS WORD AND BOTH MATTER.**

**CORRECTION 1 — this does not answer Alex.** The first version claimed it *"may dissolve half of the tier question"* and read Alex's UI/API/e2e case as an altitude-view problem. Anthony: *"I think my brother is more indicating that each tier is its own reflow2 graph that others are linked to vertically."* Alex wants SEPARATE GRAPHS PER TIER — a storage question. **The altitude view neither answers nor replaces it.** They compose: a tier-split design still wants an altitude view inside each graph.
  · **ALTITUDE** — how much detail a reader is shown. A VIEW question. No new store, no seam. *This node.*
  · **OWNERSHIP / TIER** — separate graphs, vertically linked. A STORE question. *`dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`, option (b).*
  📌 Kept on the record because an agent reading only Alex's words could build the view, declare the ask satisfied, and leave the real thing unbuilt — which is what this node nearly did.

**CORRECTION 2 — option (c) is CLOSED: the UAF/DoDAF catalogue does not belong in reflow2.** It originally proposed rendering CV-1/CV-2/CV-3/AV-1 as first-class outputs. Anthony: *"we purposefully did not define every UAF/DoDAF view as those are not appropriate for every design project AND reflow2 was meant as 'design anything' and 'build anything'… I left rendering the reflow2 graph to be able to store any design structure/content and left the agent the responsible party for 'rendering' the drawing."* **The division is deliberate: the graph stores any structure, the AGENT draws — mermaid, HTML, markdown, whatever suits.** `req:design-anything` (ACCEPTED) is what forbids binding a design-anything tool to one discipline's catalogue. See `dec:idea-a-view-that-does-not-apply-is-said-so-before-it-is-drawn` for the doctrine in full and for the idea it produced.

═══ ✅ MEASURED: TEN VIEWS EXIST, ZERO SLICE BY ALTITUDE ═══

`tools/render_views.py` renders `functional`, `flows`, `structural`, `traceability`, `released`, `decisions`, `evolution`, `provenance`, `fielded`, `budgets` — held to `dec:views-are-projections` (*"renderer fill-ins are defects"*) and `cap:bl-40` (no-extrapolation).

🛑 **EVERY ONE IS AN ASPECT VIEW: the whole design through one lens. None answers *"show me less."*** An altitude view trades depth for breadth by FILTERING what is shown — Anthony's *"exchange of breadth for depth"* done by the renderer instead of by a decomposition, and therefore **losing nothing**, since the detail stays in the graph. That is its one advantage over the tier-graph route, and it is not an argument against tier graphs, which exist for ownership reasons a view cannot supply.

📌 THE DoDAF MAPPING, KEPT AS CONTEXT AND NOT AS A BUILD TARGET (see correction 2): **CV-1 is titled "Vision"** and is the leadership-facing view with no reflow2 equivalent; **AV-1** is the executive summary; CV-2 taxonomy and CV-3 phasing are largely derivable from `Capability` + containment + Epochs, which `view_evolution` and `view_released` already partly cover. ⚠️ The exact UAF abbreviations were NOT verified against the spec and are deliberately not asserted. **The useful reading is that the MATERIAL for a leadership view is already in the graph — not that reflow2 should ship named standard views.**

═══ THE HARD PART ═══

🛑 **WHAT COMPUTES WHICH NODES ARE "TOP LEVEL"?** An altitude view is only honest if the filter derives from something the design already records. Candidates, none chosen: `Requirement.designation` (`published` vs `internal` — an audience distinction that already exists, and the strongest candidate), `priority`, `concern`, KPP status, distance from the Project root, an explicit tier property. **A filter chosen by the renderer rather than derived from the graph is precisely the "renderer fill-in" the doctrine calls a defect**, so this cannot be settled by taste.

🛑 MODELLING TRAP: `Component.level` (component → subsystem → system → system_of_systems → enterprise) is an **ASSEMBLY** ladder — *part of*. Management/vision altitude is an **ABSTRACTION** ladder. A subsystem is part of a system; a management view is not part of a worker view. Reusing `level` would make `hierarchy_issues` report nonsense.

OPTIONS.
(a) ALTITUDE VIEW DERIVED FROM AN EXISTING PROPERTY — most likely `designation`. Cheapest, no schema change, testable against the no-extrapolation standard.
(b) AN EXPLICIT TIER PROPERTY, projected on. `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` demands a computation read it, which this supplies. ⚠️ If tier GRAPHS are ever built, this property and that boundary must not disagree about what a tier is.
(c) ~~RENDER THE NAMED DoDAF VIEWS AS FIRST-CLASS OUTPUTS~~ — **CLOSED on Anthony's word.** The catalogue belongs to the agent, not to reflow2.
(d) LEAVE IT — an agent can answer "show me the top level" conversationally from `graph_report`. Counter: unrepeatable between sessions. ⚠️ Note this is NOT the same as correction 2: leaving the DRAWING to the agent is doctrine, while leaving the FILTER to the agent's judgement is a renderer fill-in. The distinction is what separates this option from (a).

📌 RELATED AND SEPARATE: `dec:idea-document-generation` and `dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph` ask what to DO with a rendered view; this asks whether the projection exists at all.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2's ten views all slice by ASPECT and none by ALTITUDE, so "show me the top level" has no projection behind it (a SEPARATE need from tier graphs, and NOT a licence to hard-code the DoDAF catalogue)
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill and corrected twice on Anthony's word within the hour — once for misreading Alex's ask as a rendering need, once for proposing that reflow2 ship the named DoDAF views. Both corrections are kept in the text rather than silently replacing it, following `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs`' precedent, because the two failure modes are worth seeing together: an agent that finds a cheaper adjacent problem and declares the original satisfied, and an agent that reaches for a familiar standard catalogue in a tool deliberately built not to have one. The second is the more likely to recur, since the catalogue is genuinely useful and the pull toward it feels like expertise rather than like a mistake. What survives both corrections is the measurement — ten aspect views, zero altitude views — and the open question of what could honestly compute the filter.
